BREAKING: Nvidia’s, $NVDA, board has created a new committee to oversee national security and export controls, days after Jensen Huang resigned over his ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chairman, will chair the committee. Nvidia’s national security and trade compliance teams will report to it.

“Advanced silicon technologies... present unprecedented challenges for national security,” said board chair Harvey Jones.

The move comes hours before Nvidia’s first earnings report since Huang’s exit.

en_summary: Canada is going through its own version of the Chat Control mess with the C-22 bill, which threatens encryption, users' privacy, and the security of digital economies. Encourages Canadians to contact senators.
text:
Canada is going through its own version of the Chat Control mess with the C-22 bill:

https://blog.mozilla.org/netpolicy/2026/10/08/canadas-bill-c-22-threatens-encryption-users-privacy-and-the-security-of-digital-economies/

Highly encourage fellow Canadians to contact senators and make clear how you feel about the importance of (backdoor-free, no asterisks) end-to-end encryption, and its benefits to a secure, free and open society.

text:
$NVDA - The U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments have released a detailed timeline of their Megaspeed investigation, confirming NVDAs topped selling to the Singapore data-center company in June 2025, when it was placed on Nvidia's internal "no sell" list. 

HERE'S WHAT THE JOINT STATEMENT REVEALS:

2024:Commerce opened an investigation after detecting suspicious activity suggesting possible diversion of sensitive U.S. semiconductors. 

May 2025: Investigators requested Nvidia's records covering direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. 

June 2025: Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal "no sell" list. June 2025: U.S. and Singaporean authorities conducted an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. 

Afterward: The Justice Department took the lead in the criminal investigation. The disclosure comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce for not placing Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist, despite support from four federal agencies. 

Importantly, Nvidia's internal "no sell" list is separate from the government's Entity List. Source: U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments

text:
The U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments have released a detailed timeline of their Megaspeed investigation, confirming $NVDA stopped selling to the Singapore data-center company in June 2025, when it was placed on Nvidia's internal "no sell" list.

Here's what the joint statement reveals:

2024: Commerce opened an investigation after detecting suspicious activity suggesting possible diversion of sensitive U.S. semiconductors.

May 2025: Investigators requested Nvidia's records covering direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed.

June 2025: Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal "no sell" list.

June 2025: U.S. and Singaporean authorities conducted an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang.

Afterward: The Justice Department took the lead in the criminal investigation.

The disclosure comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce for not placing Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist, despite support from four federal agencies.

Importantly, Nvidia's internal "no sell" list is separate from the government's Entity List.

Source: U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments

text:
I was wondering why Korean stocks were so weak today. Turns out TrendForce revised its 2027 memory demand forecasts…

TrendForce cut its demand forecasts for mobile DRAM by 0.6% and PC DRAM by 0.8%. But it raised its forecasts for server DRAM by 0.8% and graphics DRAM by 1.0%, so its forecast for total DRAM bit demand actually edged up 0.3%.

On the NAND side, TrendForce cut its total bit demand forecast by 3.2%. It lowered its estimates for mobile NAND by 6.5%, client SSDs by 10%, and enterprise SSDs by 1.5%. It now expects total NAND bit demand to grow 18.7% YoY in 2027, down from its previous forecast of 22.6%.

zh_summary: Explanation why NYC has not seen violent riots like Paris: due to NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG). Distinguishes peaceful protest as right from violent rioting as crime.
en_summary: Explanation why NYC has not seen violent riots like Paris: due to NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG). Distinguishes peaceful protest as right from violent rioting as crime.
text:
There is a reason New York City has not experienced the kind of violent riots we have witnessed in Paris and other major cities around the world.

We had the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), a specialized unit of highly trained officers prepared to confront violence before it spiraled out of control.

Let me make something absolutely clear.

Peaceful protest is a constitutional right. Violent rioting is a crime. And confusing the two is a dangerous failure of leadership.

The SRG was not created to silence peaceful protesters. It was created to protect New Yorkers when demonstrations crossed the line into violence, to protect businesses from destruction, peaceful demonstrators from violent agitators, and police officers from being assaulted.

Now City Hall is dismantling that specialized unit, introducing unarmed civilian de-escalation teams, and restricting the tools available to police.

I support de-escalation. Every responsible police officer does. But de-escalation is a strategy, not a substitute for the ability to confront violence.

You cannot reason with a brick flying through a storefront. You cannot negotiate with a Molotov cocktail. And you cannot send a social worker to do the job of a specially trained police officer confronting a violent mob.

The NYPD will still have officers responding to protests. But the question City Hall  has failed to answer is why New Yorkers will be safer without a dedicated unit specifically trained for these dangerous situations

en_summary: Commerce Department and DOJ put out unusual statement on ongoing Megaspeed investigation to set record straight, noting they don’t typically comment but public interest to provide facts and address inaccurate information. Mentions identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductors.
text:
Commerce Department and DOJ put out an unusual statement on an ongoing Megaspeed investigation to set the record straight:

“While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information
circulating in public reporting.

After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. In May 2025, Department of Commerce
investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In
June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s
investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with
Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.

Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal
investigation of Megaspeed.” 

They add:

“The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security
working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct
that may have occurred.”

Harvard Business School’s David Yoffie noted that Nvidia never had a systematic succession process.
